How binary search works

By Ada Example

Binary search finds a value in a sorted array by halving the range it looks at. It is one of the first algorithms a student learns, and it shows up in surprising places, from git bisect to database indexes.

The idea

Keep two indexes, lo and hi. Look at the middle element. If it equals the target you are done; if it is too small, throw away the left half; otherwise throw away the right half. Each step cuts the work in half, so an array of one million items needs about twenty steps.

An implementation

def search(items, target):
    lo, hi = 0, len(items) - 1
    while lo <= hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if items[mid] == target:
            return mid
        if items[mid] < target:
            lo = mid + 1
        else:
            hi = mid - 1
    return -1

Things to check

  • The array must be sorted first.
  • Compute mid without overflow in fixed-width languages.
    • Use lo + (hi - lo) / 2.
    • Never (lo + hi) / 2 with 32-bit ints.
  • Decide what to return when the target is missing.

Steps for a manual trace

  1. Write down the array.
  2. Mark lo and hi.
  3. Repeat until the marks cross.

Although the basic idea of binary search is comparatively straightforward, the details can be surprisingly tricky.
